title: Berlin Christmas Market Souvenirs - FAQ
subtitle: What to buy, what is genuine, and what gets through the airport.

items.q: Can I keep the Glühwein mug at a Berlin Christmas market?
items.a: Yes. The mug comes with a deposit (Pfand) of a few euros. Hand it back and you get the deposit returned; keep it and the deposit is what you paid for it. **WeihnachtsZauber on Gendarmenmarkt charged €3 a mug in 2025.**

items.q: How do I know a nutcracker or smoker is really from the Erzgebirge?
items.a: Look for the maker's name and the **Echt Erzgebirge, Holzkunst mit Herz** seal with a small rider on a rocking horse, used by makers certified by the Erzgebirge craft association. A figure sold as in the Erzgebirge style is not from there. A very low price is the other tell.

items.q: Can I take Glühwein home in my cabin bag?
items.a: Not in a bottle. German airports still apply **100 ml per container** in one clear 1-litre bag, and BER advises planning for that even though some of its newer lanes take more. Put bottles in a checked bag.

items.q: Is a snow globe allowed in hand luggage?
items.a: Only if it holds 100 ml or less, because the water counts as a liquid. The Ampelmann snow globe holds **115 ml**, just over the limit, so it belongs in a checked bag.

items.q: How long does a Dresdner Stollen keep?
items.a: The Dresden bakers say about **three months** somewhere cool, and a whole loaf is better after resting a week or two. The protected Dresdner Stollen carries a gold seal showing August the Strong on horseback and the EU logo.

items.q: Which Christmas souvenirs are actually made in Berlin?
items.a: Few of the market stall goods are. **KPM** makes porcelain baubles and bells in Berlin, sold at its own shop, and Ampelmann goods are designed in Berlin. Most wooden figures come from Saxony and most glass from Thuringia or Bavaria.

items.q: When do the Berlin Christmas markets open in 2026?
items.a: Most big markets open on **23 November 2026**, including Gendarmenmarkt, Schloss Charlottenburg, the Rotes Rathaus and Alexanderplatz. A few, such as the one at the Gedächtniskirche, start earlier.
